entities.name: Georgian–Armenian War
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Georgian-Armenian War (1918) was a pivotal conflict in the Caucasus region, pitting the Democratic Republic of Georgia against the First Republic of Armenia. It was sparked by the collapse of the Russian Empire and the subsequent power vacuum in the region.

This war marked a critical juncture in the history of the Caucasus, as it led to the establishment of the Soviet Union's influence in the region. The war ended in December 1918, with the signing of the Moscow Peace Treaty.

The Georgian-Armenian War had significant consequences, including the displacement of thousands of people and the redrawing of national borders. It also set the stage for the subsequent conflicts in the region, including the Soviet-Azerbaijan War.

In the words of historian Robert H. Hewsen, 'The war marked the beginning of a new era in the Caucasus, one characterized by the rise of Soviet power and the decline of traditional national identities.'
